title: Launch sequencing and orchestration for Flexible Commitment Tiers + New Instance Families
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Coordinate a phased rollout that introduces two new instance families (r4x and r5a-like) and a Flexible Commitment product tier (Flex-3 / Flex-12) across EU and APAC Dedicated offerings. This ticket sequences cross-functional tasks, finalizes release notes copy, and defines the canonical migration path and failover behavior for customers moving existing committed reservations into Flex tiers or into new instance families.

Scope:
- Productization & price table updates for Flex-3 and Flex-12 reservation SKUs.
- Launch sequencing across regions: first EU (eu-west-1 + eu-central-1), then APAC (ap-southeast-1), with a canary in eu-west-2.
- Billing backend changes for proration, swap credits, and commitment duration.
- Console UI flows for reservation swap, preview pricing, and migration warnings.
- Runbook for customer support and SRE on swap rollback and capacity overflow.

Out-of-scope: on-prem private deployments (handled by private-deploy product line).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Billing: Swap credits and proration calculations validated against 5 test cases and signed off by FIN.
2) Console: Reservation swap flow present in staging and passes usability review (DES sign-off).
3) Runtime: New instance families are routable and visible in model placement decisions (ENG validation).
4) Docs: Release notes and customer-facing FAQ published and linked in console.
5) GTM: Sales enablement pack created with migration playbook and pricing calculator.
6) Launch checklist green with SRE runbook tested during canary window.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal alpha - CLI + API only for pilot customers. Phase 1: Canary in eu-west-2 with 3 pilot customers (automatic capacity routing + billing sandbox). Phase 2: EU GA in two AZ pairs; open to self-serve for new reservations. Phase 3: APAC staged GA after capacity tests. At each phase we run smoke tests, billing reconciliation, and UX validation. If any of the top three SLO metrics (99th latency, tail token cost, reservation billing reconciliation) degrade beyond thresholds, automatically pause new reservations and rollback console swap UI via feature toggle.

risks: Billing proration edge cases when customers swap mid-billing-cycle
Insufficient canary traffic causing missed perf regressions
Console UX confusion leading to support tickets and accidental swaps
open_questions: Do we allow cross-family automated fallbacks (r4x->r5a-like) during capacity shortage? - ENG to confirm
Is there a minimum commitment for Flex-3 to prevent abuse? - FIN input needed
Should existing reservations be auto-migrated or left opt-in only? - Product decision pending
